recommendation: Keep the audit as-is. If current MolecularDefinition coordinateInterval semantics need more clarification, handle that as a MolecularDefinition-specific Clinical Genomics issue rather than resurrecting retired Sequence wording.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive Clinical Genomics request for the DSTU2 FHIR-core Sequence resource asking for a section explaining Sequence.coordinateSystem, 0-based and 1-based numbering, inclusive starts, exclusive 0-based ends, inclusive 1-based ends, and examples.
initial_application: Commit a26b8894d0c1ab993ffd7d6d0e4d4d0e4ba40c27 added the requested Sequence Coordinate System note to source/sequence/sequence-notes.xml. The same-day coordinate-family commit d830ddede2fa70d5f6ccca85e723caa4a2c7a7bf updated Sequence.coordinateSystem and start/end definitions with the same rules, and release3 history preserves that wording.
additional_context: Sequence is now listed as a removed resource, MolecularSequence is commented out, and MolecularDefinition is the active Clinical Genomics successor. FHIR-51227 and later source history replaced MolecularSequence with MolecularDefinition, whose coordinateInterval/CodeableConcept model is different from the old integer Sequence.coordinateSystem model.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. Copying the 2016 Sequence prose into MolecularDefinition would be a new model-specific decision, not reconciliation of FHIR-11233.
